newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds add to recent gains as rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Bunds add to recent gains as rate fears ease.

text.p: Bund futures continued a series of gains on Tuesday amid signs the Bundesbank will not soon be forced to lift interest rates.
The DTB Bund future was up 16 basis points at 102.89 in late afternoon trade after having traded as high as 102.92.
Traders said that while the contract faces resistance at 103.00, they believe the market's recent strength shows that further gains are likely.
"I think this week the trend will continue higher," one Frankfurt trader said. "It looks positive."
Traders, however, were reluctant to take bold positions ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting, results of which are due at around 1815 GMT.
Domestically, traders are regaining confidence the Bundesbank will not soon raise interest rates and are willing to take fresh long positions.

The Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development added to the latest rate optimism, saying conditions for low interest rates and economic growth in Germany would remain intact this year and next.
M3, which came in lower than expected, also added to the bullish mood, slowing to an annualised rate of 5.7 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June. Economists had forecast 6.3 percent growth.

"This is very nice for the Bundesbank as it means they can hold off on an interest rate move for the time being. They can have a nice relaxed Bundesbank meeting on Thursday," said Gerhard Grebe, chief economist at Bank Julius Baer.
With M3 out of the way, the market's focus will turn to the Ifo business sentiment index, due for release at 0800 GMT on Wednesday.
According to a Reuter poll of economists, the Ifo index should rise to 96.6 in July from 96.00.
The benchmark cash 10-year Bund climbed to 103.07 from 102.78 to yield 5.58 percent.
